body:
> Found 2026-09-01: an operator session ran `hkb up --serve` in `pipao-v2` while a server from a *different*
> checkout was already up on 4666 — and already serving pipao's board. It got told "port 4666 is already in use
> — pass --port <n>, or stop the other hkb serve", followed that advice, and started a second server on 4667.
> Two servers now poll the same two boards.

## Why

`hkb serve` is **multi-board by design**. It reads `~/.config/hkb/boards.json`, and one process serves every
registered checkout — the log says so out loud: `hkb serve on http://127.0.0.1:4666 — 2 boards`, listing both.
So the second server was not merely redundant; the board it was started for was *already on screen*.

The reason nobody could tell is that the two halves of the state live at different levels and nothing joins them:

| what | where | scope |
|---|---|---|
| which boards a server shows | `~/.config/hkb/boards.json` | **user-level** — knows every checkout |
| whether a server is running | `.kanban/serve.pid` | **per-checkout** — knows only its own |

`portInUse` (`src/serve.js:642`) reads the *per-checkout* pid file. From pipao that file does not exist, so the
check falls through to the generic message, whose two suggestions — a second server, or stop the other one —
are the two worst answers available. The one that was true is not among them.

`hkb up` promises idempotence: "run it twice and the second run reports what is already running and starts
nothing." That promise holds per checkout and silently does not hold across checkouts, which is precisely the
case a multi-board server exists to serve.

The cost is small but it is waste by accident: two processes polling two boards each, where one was covering
both. Value 2 is frugality, and conditional `GET`s being cheap is not a reason to make twice as many.

## What

- **A user-level serve record.** `~/.config/hkb/serve.json` (beside the registry it belongs with):
  `{ pid, url, boards: [...], started_at }`, written by `serve` at startup and removed on exit — the same
  lifecycle `writeServeUrl`/`dropServeUrl` (#204) already implement per checkout. That card built the per-board
  half; this is the same idea one level up, and the two should share code rather than diverge.
- **`hkb up --serve` consults it before spawning.** If a live server already covers this board, print its URL
  and start nothing — the idempotence `up` already promises, extended to the scope `serve` actually operates at.
  A stale record (pid gone) is ignored, exactly as a stale pid file is.
- **`portInUse` says the true thing.** When the port's holder is a live hkb serve that covers this board:
  "already serving this board at <url>". When it covers other boards but not this one: name the fix that
  actually works — register this checkout, or `--port`. Only when it is not hkb at all should it say what it
  says today.
- **`hkb up --status` should say which server covers this board**, whether or not this checkout started it. An
  operator asking "is my board up" is not asking "did *this directory* start a process".
- **Decide, do not assume:** whether a second server should be refused outright or merely reported. There are
  real reasons for two (different `--host`, one exposed and one loopback), so refusing outright may be wrong —
  but the default should not be reached by accident, and `--port` should stay the deliberate escape.

**Not this card:** which boards a server shows is the registry's job and already works; #170 covers keeping a
worker's checkout out of it.

## Done when

- [ ] A live server records itself where any checkout can see it, and removes the record on exit.
- [ ] `hkb up --serve` in a checkout whose board is already served prints that server's URL and spawns nothing.
- [ ] `portInUse` distinguishes "already serving this board", "an hkb serve that does not cover this board", and
      "not hkb at all", with the right fix on each.
- [ ] `hkb up --status` names the server covering this board even when another checkout started it.
- [ ] A stale record never blocks a legitimate start, with a test.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass; the web-board wiki page describes the record and the one-server rule.
goal: A live server records itself where any checkout can see it; hkb up --serve prints that URL and spawns nothing when this board is already served; portInUse tells the three cases apart with the right fix on each; up --status names the server covering this board whoever started it
title: hkb up --serve starts a second server for a board an existing server is already showing, because the pid file is per checkout and the board registry is not
